title: Health Economics for Therapists — Cost-Effectiveness Basics

hook.en: A treatment that works but costs a month's salary will not help most patients. Money, time and therapists are limited everywhere, so every choice to do one thing means not doing another. Health economics gives therapists a plain language for these choices, and the numbers to back it.
hook.ur: Jo ilaaj kaam karta hai lekin mahine ki tankhwah jitna kharch karta hai woh zyada tar mareezon ki madad nahi karega. Paisa, waqt aur therapists har jagah mehdood hain, isliye ek kaam karne ka matlab doosra na karna hai. Health economics therapists ko in faislon ke liye saadi zubaan aur unki himayat ke numbers deti hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain opportunity cost, tell cost-minimisation, cost-effectiveness and cost-utility apart, calculate and read an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), understand QALYs, and ask the right economic questions of a study.
goal.ur: End tak aap opportunity cost samjhayenge, cost-minimisation, cost-effectiveness aur cost-utility mein farq karenge, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) nikal kar parhenge, QALYs samjhenge, aur kisi study se sahi maashi sawal poochhenge.

text.en: **Opportunity cost** is what you give up when you choose one option: the money or time could have bought something else. An **economic evaluation** compares both **costs and outcomes** of two or more options. **Cost-minimisation** compares costs when outcomes are the same. **Cost-effectiveness** measures cost per unit of a natural outcome (for example, per fall prevented). **Cost-utility** measures cost per **quality-adjusted life year (QALY)**, which combines length and quality of life. The **ICER** is the extra cost of a new option divided by its extra benefit compared with the alternative.
text.ur: **Opportunity cost** woh hai jo aap ek option chunne par chhodte hain: woh paisa ya waqt kuch aur khareed sakta tha. **Economic evaluation** do ya zyada options ke **kharch aur nateejon** dono ka muqabla karti hai. **Cost-minimisation** kharch ka muqabla karti hai jab nateeje ek jaise hon. **Cost-effectiveness** kisi qudrati nateeje ki ek ikai par kharch naapti hai (masalan ek girna rokne par). **Cost-utility** **quality-adjusted life year (QALY)** par kharch naapti hai, jo zindagi ki lambai aur quality ko milati hai. **ICER** naye option ka mazeed kharch, mutabadil ke muqabale mein uske mazeed faide se taqseem hai.

text.en: Think of **buying a motorbike or a car** for a family. You compare the price (cost) and what you get: seats, safety, fuel (benefit). A car costs more but carries five people more safely. Whether it is "worth it" depends on how much extra you pay for each extra benefit, and on what else the money could buy. That is cost-effectiveness.
text.ur: Ghar ke liye **motorbike ya car khareedna** sochein. Aap qeemat (kharch) aur jo milta hai (seatein, hifazat, petrol, faida) ka muqabla karte hain. Car zyada mehngi hai lekin paanch logon ko zyada mehfooz le jati hai. "Qeemat wasool" hai ya nahi yeh is par hai ke har mazeed faide ke liye aap kitna mazeed dete hain, aur paisa aur kya khareed sakta tha. Yehi cost-effectiveness hai.

question.en: A new balance programme costs 4,000 rupees more per person and prevents 0.05 more falls per person than usual care. What is the cost per fall prevented?
question.ur: Naya balance programme usual care se per shakhs 4,000 rupay zyada kharch karta hai aur per shakhs 0.05 zyada girne rokta hai. Ek girna rokne ka kharch kitna hai?

text.en: 80,000 rupees per fall prevented (4,000 divided by 0.05), which is the ICER
text.ur: Ek girna rokne par 80,000 rupay (4,000 ko 0.05 se taqseem), jo ICER hai

feedback.en: Yes — extra cost divided by extra benefit.
feedback.ur: Haan — mazeed kharch ko mazeed faide se taqseem.

feedback.en: The division is the other way round.
That is the extra cost per person, not per fall.
feedback.ur: Yeh per shakhs mazeed kharch hai, per girna nahi.

text.en: **Counting only the clinic's costs.** The patient's costs (transport, lost wages, helpers) and society's costs (time off work, later complications) may be larger than the fee. And a result in one health system may not travel to another: prices, wages and care pathways differ. Also remember that "cost-effective" depends on how much society is willing to pay, which is a value judgement, not a fact in the data.
text.ur: **Sirf clinic ke kharch ginna.** Mareez ke kharch (aamad-o-raft, khoyi hui ujrat, madadgar) aur samaj ke kharch (kaam se chhutti, baad ke masail) fees se zyada ho sakte hain. Aur ek nizam-e-sehat ka nateeja doosre tak nahi pohanchta: qeematein, ujratein aur care ke raaste mukhtalif hain. Yeh bhi yaad rakhein ke "cost-effective" is par hai ke samaj kitna dene ko tayyar hai, jo qadar ka faisla hai, data ka haqeeqat nahi.

text.en: **Count what an extra session really costs.** Add your time, the room, the equipment, the patient's travel and time off work, and the cost of repeat visits. Compare a clinic-based programme with a home programme with phone calls: you may find that fewer clinic visits give the same result at lower total cost, and that patients prefer it. Use this when you argue for a service with managers.
text.ur: **Dekhein ke ek mazeed session ka asal kharch kya hai.** Apna waqt, kamra, aala, mareez ka safar aur kaam se chhutti, aur dobara visits ka kharch jodein. Clinic wale programme ka phone calls ke saath ghar ke programme se muqabla karein: ho sakta hai kam clinic visits kam kul kharch par wahi nateeja dein, aur mareez ise pasand karein. Managers se kisi khidmat ke liye daleel dete waqt isay istemal karein.

question.en: Why do health economists talk about "willingness to pay"?
question.ur: Health economists "adaigi ki aamadgi" ki baat kyun karte hain?

answer.en: Because budgets are limited, a decision-maker needs a rule for how much extra cost is acceptable for each extra unit of health. Some countries use a threshold per QALY. If an ICER is below that threshold, the option is usually seen as good value. Thresholds differ between countries and are debated, because they reflect values about fairness, not just arithmetic.
answer.ur: Kyunke budget mehdood hain, faisla karne wale ko aise qaide ki zaroorat hai ke sehat ki har mazeed ikai ke liye kitna mazeed kharch qabil-e-qubool hai. Kuch mulk per QALY ek had istemal karte hain. Agar ICER us had se neeche ho to option aam taur par achhi qeemat samjha jata hai. Hadein mulkon mein mukhtalif hain aur un par bahas hoti hai, kyunke yeh insaaf ke baare mein qadron ko zahir karti hain, sirf hisab ko nahi.

beats.patient: A clinic compares usual twice-weekly clinic exercise with a home programme plus two phone calls for knee osteoarthritis. Pain improves equally in both. The clinic programme costs 9,000 rupees per patient (including travel and lost work), the home programme 3,500.
beats.assessment: Outcomes are similar, so this is a cost-minimisation situation: the home programme is cheaper for the same result.
beats.treatment: The clinic offers the home programme to suitable patients and keeps clinic sessions for those who need hands-on care or have complex problems.
beats.reassess: More patients are served at the same budget, waiting times fall and satisfaction is similar.

text.en: **Money must never override safety.** A cheaper option is not acceptable if it exposes patients to harm or leaves out essential care. Economic analyses should include the costs of adverse events and should not hide groups who do worse. When resources are scarce, be open with patients about choices and involve them in decisions.
text.ur: **Paisa safety par kabhi haavi nahi hona chahiye.** Sasta option qabil-e-qubool nahi agar mareezon ko nuqsan ka khatra de ya zaroori care chhor de. Maashi tajziyon mein adverse events ke kharch shamil hone chahiyen aur un groups ko nahi chhupana chahiye jo kharab nateeja dein. Jab wasail kam hon to mareezon se choice ke baare mein khul kar baat karein aur unhein faislon mein shamil karein.

text.en: Drummond and colleagues' standard text sets out the methods of economic evaluation of health care programmes, defining the main types (cost-minimisation, cost-effectiveness, cost-utility and cost-benefit analysis) and stressing a clear perspective (patient, health system or society), costs and outcomes measured over the same time horizon, and discounting of future costs and benefits. The CHEERS 2022 statement lists 28 items that should be reported in an economic evaluation, including the study perspective, the comparators, how costs and outcomes were measured and the handling of uncertainty.
text.ur: Drummond aur saathiyon ki mayaari kitab sehat ke programmes ke maashi tajziye ke tareeqe batati hai, mukhya qismein (cost-minimisation, cost-effectiveness, cost-utility aur cost-benefit analysis) tay karti hai, aur saaf nuqta-e-nazar (mareez, nizam-e-sehat ya samaj), ek hi waqt ke ufaq mein naape gaye kharch aur nateeje, aur mustaqbil ke kharch aur faide par discounting par zor deti hai. CHEERS 2022 statement 28 items batata hai jo maashi tajziye mein report hone chahiye, jin mein study ka nuqta-e-nazar, muqabla karne wale options, kharch aur nateeje kaise naape gaye aur be-yaqeeni ka intizam shamil hain.

text.en: **Cost, Benefit, Compare, Perspective.** Count all costs, measure the benefit, compare with the alternative and state whose point of view.
text.ur: **Kharch, Faida, Muqabla, Nuqta-e-nazar.** Tamam kharch ginein, faida naapein, mutabadil se muqabla karein aur batayein kis ka nuqta-e-nazar.

summary.en: Economic evaluation compares costs and outcomes of options; opportunity cost is what you give up by choosing.
summary.ur: Maashi tajziya options ke kharch aur nateejon ka muqabla karta hai; opportunity cost woh hai jo aap chunne par chhodte hain.

summary.en: ICER is extra cost divided by extra benefit; QALYs combine length and quality of life.
summary.ur: ICER mazeed kharch ko mazeed faide se taqseem hai; QALYs zindagi ki lambai aur quality milate hain.

summary.en: Count patient and society costs too, and never let cost override safety.
summary.ur: Mareez aur samaj ke kharch bhi ginein, aur kharch ko safety par kabhi haavi na hone dein.
